note: The same world, but the two asset sources are binding names the Worker does not bind: one that was never a binding at all and one that is audit-only and never reaches the Worker. Both must FAIL, because a source that names a binding nobody binds sends an auditor after a binding that is not there.

manifest.policy: Fixture policy: this world declares the files above and the one command above, and the evaluator must accept every claim because each one points at something the fixture actually contains.

control_registry.contract: The fixture gate is the command a release would run for this world, and it is what makes the one control on this boundary reviewable.

capabilities.title: Fixture inbound boundary
capabilities.owner: the fixture obligation that owns the inbound boundary of the synthetic world
capabilities.authority: The fixture's own rule: a boundary is only a boundary when it crosses the boundary zone and carries at least one control
capabilities.summary: A synthetic caller crosses one declared boundary into a synthetic handler, and the model says so with artefacts that exist.

assets.description: A synthetic key the caller presents; the ledger names the binding it would come from, and the name is one the Worker never binds.
A synthetic operator-visible record the fixture writes through a redacting logger; the ledger points it at an audit-only name, which is never bound to the Worker.

boundaries.crosses: The synthetic inbound boundary an unverified request crosses before any handler runs.
The synthetic logging boundary an internal failure crosses on its way to an operator-visible record.

threats.scenario: A synthetic caller presents a key it does not own, and the handler cannot tell the forgery from the genuine request.

mitigations.note: The fixture suite refuses the unknown key before any handler runs.

review_items: Does the synthetic handler still refuse an unknown key before it reads any state?
Can the synthetic log record carry a value the caller supplied?
